primary.summary_en: Saint Stephen is commemorated as the first Christian martyr, whose death by stoning marked the beginning of the Church's witness through blood. Celebrated on the day after Christmas, this Feast highlights the connection between the Incarnation and the sacrifice required to defend the faith. He is traditionally honored as the patron of deacons, reflecting his role as the first among the seven chosen to serve the community.
primary.body_en: The liturgy for the Feast of Saint Stephen places the martyrdom of the proto-martyr immediately following the celebration of the Nativity, illustrating that the birth of Christ brings with it the call to witness. According to the Acts of the Apostles, Stephen was one of the first deacons, known for his wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke. His defense of the faith before the Sanhedrin culminated in a vision of the glory of God, for which he was stoned to death outside the city walls. This event serves as a powerful reminder that following Christ involves a total surrender of self, a theme central to the Christian vocation. As the first to die for his faith, Stephen set a precedent for all future martyrs, demonstrating that the light of Christ shines brightest in the darkness of persecution.
primary.confidence_note_en: The Feast is fixed in the universal liturgical calendar of the Roman Rite and is explicitly listed in the USCCB calendar for 2026 as a Feast.

app_hooks.prayer_prompt_en: Grant us the courage to witness to the truth, as Saint Stephen did in his final moments.
